chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily God, Mighty and Majestic, says: The mutual discussion of knowledge among My servants is from what revives the dead hearts, when they end up in it toward My command.'

key_terms.أَمْرِي: My command — referring to God's divine commands, the shariah and religious obligations
key_terms.الْقُلُوبُ الْمَيِّتَةُ: The spiritually dead hearts — those hardened by heedlessness and distance from God
key_terms.تَذَاكُرُ الْعِلْمِ: The mutual discussion or sharing of knowledge — an active, reciprocal process between learners

ai.seo_question: How does discussing knowledge revive spiritually dead hearts according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith is a divine saying (hadith qudsi) in which Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates from the Prophet (SAWW) who conveys God's own words. God declares that when believers discuss and exchange knowledge with one another, this spiritual discourse is a means of reviving hearts that have become spiritually dead. The hadith emphasizes that the ultimate purpose of knowledge discussion must lead toward God's commands — not intellectual exercise alone — making the revitalization of the heart conditional on its alignment with divine guidance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “The discussion of the knowledge between My<sup>azwj</sup> servants is from what the dead hearts are revived upon. When, as a consequence, they end up in it to My<sup>azwj</sup> Commands”’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The Holy Prophet said, ‘Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious says, ‘The discussions of the scholars among My servants are of the matters that bring the dead hearts to life if they come to and end up to My commandments.’”
